dishes.name: Boles de picolat
dishes.desc: Catalan meatballs of minced beef and pork with bacon, garlic, parsley and bread soaked in milk, simmered in tomato sauce, often with white beans. A classic of Roussillon home cooking.

dishes.name: Rousquilles
dishes.desc: Ring-shaped Catalan biscuits coated in a thin, sweet, lightly aniseed white glaze. A symbol of Perpignan pastry, found in bakeries all over French Catalonia.

dishes.name: Crème catalane
dishes.desc: A custard flavoured with cinnamon and lemon zest under a hard caramelised sugar crust, like a crème brûlée. The standard Catalan dessert on Perpignan menus.

dishes.name: Bunyetes
dishes.desc: Very thin, crisp, round fritters scented with orange blossom and citrus, made on the Roussillon plain and in the Vallespir and Conflent. Traditionally an Easter treat.

dishes.name: Collioure anchovies
dishes.desc: Anchovies fished at night from boats with a lamp, then salted for months. Collioure on the Côte Vermeille is known for them, eaten on bread or with escalivada.
